purchase objective.

4750E35ABF6A44C1B7818CBD287621DB.description:
Describe how technological developments, societal decisions, and
personal practices affect sustainability in the United States.

0E410A9E88BB4154AF33D68EC2348566.description:
Describe how physical, human, and political features influence
events, movements, and adaptation to the environment.

165DE526229E4824B0C258C5A195B8CE.description:
Investigate the effects of exploration, conquest, exploitation, and
colonial settlement on Indigenous Tribes in at least two
geographic regions.

157FC1BD81CD4CAA9235B246A933C185.description:
Trace on a map Indigenous Tribes' encounters with Europeans in
North America and the Caribbean Islands in the 15th through the
18th centuries.

C1FF7786293C41EAB53454E4978F5733.description:
Investigate the causes behind domestic and global migration,
distinguishing between voluntary relocation and forced
displacement, including scenarios like refugees, individuals
compelled to leave their homeland and those enslaved.

20687A8D37E74AE2AAC85F408E8C7713.description:
Identify and analyze the implications and ramifications for Native
American Tribes of the movement of people, goods, ideas, and
cultural patterns to what became the United States, considering
past, present, and future trends.

Locate and examine significant physical geographic features of
the thirteen British colonies that became the United States.

Locate states, capital cities, and important geographic features on
a United States map.

Use geographic tools such as maps, satellite images, photographs,
and other representations to investigate and compare the
process of constructing, recognizing, and utilizing, boundaries and
borders (geographic and/or human-made) in the United States.

Explain specific protections provided in the Bill of Rights to individuals
and the importance of these amendments to the ratification of the U.S.
Constitution.

Analyze the Preamble and sections of the Constitution to
understand the establishment and limitations of democratic
principles.
Note: Teachers may choose the section of the Constitution that
are most accessible and relevant for their classroom.

Examine and critique how colonial and new states’ governments
established, expanded, limited, or denied rights and
responsibilities of specific groups and individuals with particular
attention to citizens, enslaved peoples, foreigners, nobles,
religious groups, women, class systems, and Tribes.

67482602F2854870B6422F0870EC1BF1.description:
Analyze how cooperation and conflict among people contribute to
political, economic, religious, and current social events and
situations in the United States.

874F7667A63C42B2A5BE021E91C9A08E.description:
Analyze the significance of the decisions and laws of the newly
formed federal and state governments in establishing, expanding,
limiting, and denying rights to individuals 1789-1865.

69C3CD74B91D441FAB777BBF01EFEF75.description:
Compare and contrast how the governments of the British
monarchy, American colonies, and Indigenous Tribes shaped
interactions with one another.

document.title: 2024 Oregon Social Science Standards

Use primary and secondary sources to identify the important
characteristics of civilizations and cultures in Sub-Saharan
Africa.

Use primary and secondary sources to identify the important
characteristics of civilizations and cultures in Western Asia,
the Middle East, and North Africa from Paleolithic to 1500.

Use primary and secondary sources to identify
archaeological evidence of the characteristics of Indigenous
civilizations of the Americas and Caribbean basin from the
Paleolithic to 1500.

Identify the motivations and methods governments and
other institutions use to create, reinforce, or address
injustice and divisions in society.

Investigate the historical origins and modern manifestations
of anti-Judaism.
Note: Anti-Judaism refers to the bias, discrimination, and
violence experienced by Jewish individuals and communities
throughout history primarily rooted in religious identity.
Antisemitism is the prejudice, discrimination, hostility, or
violence directed toward Jewish people or communities and
their religious, cultural, and ethnic identity.

Compare and contrast the central tenets and cultural
practices of Hinduism, Judaism, Buddhism, Taoism,
Christianity, and Islam.

Identify the key components of creation or origin stories
from various civilizations and cultures.

Compare the origins and development of early world
religions from the Neolithic to 1500 CE.

DAB44BDC2A0F4A0DA58A9691D9913D23.description:
Identify and describe examples of how conquest and
colonialism affected historically underrepresented identities,
cultures, and communities.

1A7C97896C1F42FCA4CADF834D30EE60.description:
Identify examples of historical and contemporary indigenous
resilience and resistance to colonial exploration and
settlement.

48B1C53F1717496C86A665C2B3C88DE0.description:
Use primary and secondary sources to identify and analyze
the interactions and exchanges of cultures and civilizations
after 600 CE.

591711480EDC492E872C59910B1E711D.description:
Use primary and secondary sources to identify and analyze
the interactions and exchanges of cultures and civilizations
from the Neolithic to 900 CE.

8F84B7406D2C4CE19940042E9925854A.description:
Describe the key features and developments of
independently formed civilizations and cultures between the
Neolithic and 900 CE.

336E457A5CF14C4DA56C968ACF5F94FE.description:
Explain the characteristics historians and social scientists
have used to define complex societies or “civilizations.”
Note- The characteristics remain a topic of debate for
historians and archeologists and some societies do not
include all listed characteristics.

F81262B1A1FE40199CB96003EF39E01F.description:
Construct and interpret a timeline using words and
abbreviations for identifying key periods in the development
of human societies.

75F9A178AA5C4287A6005A30CA1119B6.description:
Explain how growing interdependence and technological
advances improve living standards within and across
societies.

7801ABA0416C403D8EC76396D0F58C0A.description:
Analyze the effect on the costs of goods and services for
trade or barter with the development of specialization in
local economies.

Compare specialization and trade in two or more civilizations
or empires.

Evaluate alternative approaches or solutions to economic
issues in terms of benefits and costs for traditionally
underrepresented groups and individuals in early major
Western and non-Western civilizations.

Explain how government interventions, such as incentives,
taxes or tribute affect individual participation in the
economy.

the production, distribution, and consumption of resources.

markets.

Explain how supply and demand affect wages and prices of
resources.

locally relevant living expenses and savings for various
income levels.

least two student selected career choices.

Identify and describe examples of how conquest and
colonialism affected traditionally underrepresented
identities, cultures, and communities.

Identify how physical environments influence and effect
changes in population, technical advancements, culture, and
approaches to resource use, stewardship, and sustainability
from the Paleolithic to 900 CE.

Identify and explain the consequences of cultural conflict,
interaction, exchange, and/or fusion.

5F26E25F4552428A9582B853A03242AD.description:
Identify and describe how the physical geography and
human characteristics of places influence cultural attributes
such as politics, law, religion, diet, architecture, and the
construction of race, ethnicity, and gender.

and communication affected interactions between human
settlements, including the diffusion of ideas and cultural
practices.

countries, capitals, other cities, and important bodies of
water to describe, place, region, and the absolute location
and relative location of cultures and civilizations.

technologies, and spatial thinking to compare how physical
geography, human, and environmental characteristics of a
region influenced the movement of people, goods, and ideas
among civilizations and empires.

EAF94187DEE14C7EB6AA0E2AB9920BD9.description: Navigate and negotiate offers of employment including human resource paperwork.

6EB9D6396CE945D1B871FE795BD7728A.description: Explore how personal strengths, aptitudes, interests and values connect with future career paths.
